The layer’s Fill & Stroke section still holds stacked paints, noise and blending for the whole text layer. Text doesn’t take image fills.
Underline and strikethrough aren’t drawn on gradient characters. Color emoji in a gradient range have no outline to fill. Other apps and older Mica versions get one stand-in color.

tips: Apply the gradient to the word you want it across; applying it to the whole layer stretches it over every line.
Choose a solid color to replace a gradient on the selected characters.
Gradients show live while you edit, so you can adjust stops and see the result in place.

features.title: Fonts and typography features
features.summary: Use any installed font, variable font axes and OpenType features. Fonts travel with your board.
steps: Select text and open the font picker in Typography to choose any installed family and style.
For variable fonts, adjust the axes such as weight or width with the sliders.
Turn on OpenType features such as small caps, tabular numbers or alternates.
Set Rendering to Smooth (default) or Sharp for hard pixel edges.

faq.q: Will my board look right on another device?
faq.a: Yes. Fonts used on a board are embedded with it and registered when it opens.

faq.q: Why does text look softer when zoomed in?
faq.a: It sharpens as you zoom; Scale with Box text keeps a fixed resolution.

features.why: Mica uses the fonts installed on your device, plus font files you add to a board or your Font Library. Embedded fonts travel with the board, so it looks the same on your other devices and for anyone who opens a .refboard.
uses: Set a brand typeface on a board and keep it on every device.
Use tabular numbers for prices and tables so digits line up.
Fine-tune weight and width on a variable font.
Turn off antialiasing for pixel fonts with Sharp rendering.

details.text: Searchable, with each family previewed in its own face. Sections: In This Board, Font Library and All Fonts.

Embeds .ttf, .otf, .ttc or .otc files in the board. You can also drop font files on the canvas. Up to 40 MB per file and 64 faces per board. Remove from Board takes a family out again. Both are undoable.

The Fonts screen in the library sidebar (on iPhone, a page of the Assets tab) imports many fonts or whole folders at once, up to 2,000 files per import. Picking a library family in a board embeds that family in the board.
A slider for each axis of the first selected layer’s font, such as weight, width or optical size. Reset Axes returns them to the font’s defaults.

Ligatures, Kerning, Discretionary Ligatures, Tabular, Proportional, Old-Style and Lining Numbers, Fractions, Slashed Zero, Small Caps, Capitals to Small Caps, Case-Sensitive Forms, Superscript, Subscript, Stylistic Alternates and Stylistic Sets 1–5. The list shows what the font supports when it reports that.
Smooth (default) gives antialiased edges. Sharp turns antialiasing off for hard pixel edges, on the canvas and in export.
Fonts register for Mica only, never system-wide. On a device without a family that isn’t embedded, text falls back to the system font.

tips: Embed any font that isn’t a system font before you share or export a board.
Use Tabular Numbers for columns of figures and Case-Sensitive Forms for all-caps headings.
Check the license before you embed a font in a board you share.
Features that change the number of glyphs, such as ligatures, appear after you finish editing.

features.title: Shapes
features.summary: Draw rectangles, ovals, triangles, polygons, stars and lines, then edit their corners, fill and stroke.
steps: Choose a shape from the Shapes menu or the Pencil palette, then drag on the canvas.
Hold Shift for equal proportions, or Option to draw from the center.
Set the corner radius in the inspector; it stays the same when you resize.
Use Convert to Path when you want to edit the points.

faq.q: Why doesn’t my new shape have an outline?
faq.a: New filled shapes start without a stroke. Turn on Stroke in the tool options or add one in Fill & Stroke.

faq.q: Can I edit stroke dashes and caps?
faq.a: Yes. Stroke options include position, cap, join and dash.

features.why: Shapes are the basic vector building blocks for icons, buttons, cards and diagrams. They keep their parameters, such as corner radius, side count and arc, so you can change them later instead of redrawing.
uses: Draw a rounded button background with iOS-style smooth corners.
Make a pie chart slice or a progress ring from an oval.
Draw a hexagon badge with a polygon and adjust its sides.
Add dashed outlines to mark areas on a wireframe.

details.text: Rectangle R, Oval O, Star S, Triangle ⇧R, Polygon ⇧O, Line ⇧L, Pen P. Hold Shift for equal proportions or 45° angles, and Option to draw from the center.

One radius for every corner, or separate top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left values. Radii stay the same when you resize, and overlapping radii shrink together so they stay inside the box. Frames take corner radii too.
Figma-style continuous corners from 0 to 100 % on rectangles and frames. The iOS button sets 60 %.

details.term: Oval: Arc Start, Arc Sweep and Ratio
details.text: Start and sweep from 0 to 360° make pies and arcs. Ratio from 0 to 99 % cuts a hole for rings.
From 3 to 60, with a corner radius. The Triangle and Polygon tools both draw polygons.
Drag the handles on a selected shape to change its radius, side count, arc or ring ratio directly.

New filled shapes start without a stroke; turn on Stroke in the tool options. Stroke Position (Center, Inside, Outside), Cap (Flat, Round, Square), Join (Miter, Round, Bevel) and Dashed with Dash Length and Dash Gap.

In the inspector and the right-click menu, for rectangles, ovals, triangles, polygons, stars, blobs, arrows and older closed shapes. Opens the result in point editing; fill, stroke and effects are kept. One undo step.

tips: Keep shapes as shapes as long as you can; convert to a path only when you need to move individual points.
Use Inside stroke position on buttons and cards so the outline doesn’t grow the shape.
Use 60 % Corner Smoothing for app icons and iOS-style controls.
Use the Scale tool (K) when you want strokes, radii and shadows to scale with the shape.

features.title: Generators
features.summary: Make placeholder text, waves, QR codes, color harmonies, charts and curved text on your device, as ordinary editable layers.
steps: Open Quick Actions and choose Generators, or choose Design Tools → Insert. On Mac, choose Insert → Generators….
Pick a tab: Content, Waves, QR Code, Palette, Chart or Arc Text. The preview updates as you change settings.
On the Content tab, choose a type such as Lorem Sentence, Full Name or Email. With text layers selected, Fill Text gives each a different value; otherwise Add Text adds one.
On the other tabs, choose Insert. The result appears at the center of the view, selected, in one undo step.

faq.q: Can I edit Arc Text as text later?
faq.a: No. It’s inserted as one filled vector shape. Change the text in the generator and insert it again.

faq.q: How do I draw an arrow between two layers?
faq.a: Select exactly two layers and choose Connect with Arrow, or press ⌃⌥A. The arrow doesn’t follow the layers when they move.

faq.q: Do generators need a connection?
faq.a: No. Everything is made on your device.

features.why: Generators replace a handful of popular design plugins with built-in tools. They run on your device, need no account or connection, and make ordinary layers you can keep editing.
uses: Fill a UI mockup's text layers with realistic names, emails and prices in one step.
Add a scannable QR code to a poster or slide.
Build a quick color harmony from one brand color.
Sketch a bar or donut chart shape for a dashboard mockup.

details.text: Opened from Quick Actions, Design Tools → Insert, or Insert → Generators… on Mac. Tabs: Content, Blobs, Stars, Waves, QR Code, Palette, Chart and Arc Text; Blobs and Stars open their own studios. Results land at the center of the view, selected, in one undo step.

17 types: Lorem Words, Lorem Sentence, Lorem Paragraph, Full Name, First Name, Email, Phone Number, Company, Job Title, City, Date, Time, Price, Percentage, Whole Number, Username and Web Address. Fill Text gives each selected text or sticky layer a different value and keeps its formatting; with nothing selected, Add Text adds a new text layer. Shuffle picks new values. Emails and phone numbers are fictional.
Smooth, Peaks or Stepped style, Width, Height, 1–5 Bands, Wave Count (1–24), Amplitude and Color. Back bands sit higher and lighter; the front band uses the chosen color.
Link or Text up to 1,200 bytes, Error Correction (Low, Medium, Quartile, High), Color, Size and an optional White Quiet Zone. Inserted as a vector drawing.

A Base Color plus a Harmony: Complementary, Analogous, Triadic, Split Complementary, Tetradic, Monochromatic or Shades. Adds one palette card per color, selected together. Palette generation needs Mica Pro.

Vertical Bars, Horizontal Bars, Line, Area, Pie or Donut from typed Data Values separated by commas, spaces or lines (up to 48; invalid numbers are skipped). Colors follow the chosen color. Shapes only, with no text labels.
Text, Weight, Color, Size, Letter Spacing and Bend from −100% to +100%; a full bend wraps the text into a circle. Inserted as one filled vector, not editable text.

With exactly two layers selected: Quick Actions, Design Tools → Insert, Insert on Mac, or ⌃⌥A. Draws an editable arrow between their edges with an 8 pt gap. It doesn't follow the layers when they move.

tips: Select all the text layers in a list before choosing Fill Text so each gets a different value.
Keep strong contrast and the White Quiet Zone on QR codes so cameras can scan them.
Type your arc text carefully; once inserted it is a shape, so fix typos in the generator.
Recolor waves and charts later with the ordinary fill controls.
Use Shuffle to try new variations before inserting.

features.title: Blobs and stars
features.summary: Generate organic blobs and stars that stay editable after you insert them.
steps: Open the Shapes menu in the tool dock and choose Blobs… or Stars…. They’re also in Design Tools → Insert.
In Blobs, pick a style such as Organic, Cloud, Goo or Ring, then adjust its controls, Randomness, Rotation and Symmetry. Choose Shuffle for a new variation.
In Stars, pick a preset such as Classic Star or Sparkle, or set Points, Inner Radius and Roundness.
Choose Filled or Outlined and a color. For blobs, set Count and Arrangement to insert up to 24 at once.
Choose Insert. Select a blob or star later to edit it in the Blob or Star section of the inspector.

faq.q: Can I move the points by hand?
faq.a: Yes. Choose Convert to Path from the right-click menu or the inspector. The outline stays; the blob or star controls are removed.

faq.q: Does resizing a blob reset it?
faq.a: No. A blob redraws inside its new size, and later tweaks keep that size.

features.why: Blobs and Stars generate decorative shapes that would take a long time to draw by hand. Unlike flat imports, each one keeps its settings, so you can restyle, reshuffle or resize it after it's on the board.
uses: Add organic background shapes behind a poster headline or app screenshot.
Scatter a cluster of blobs as a pattern for a social graphic.
Make sale badges, sparkles and starbursts for marketing layouts.
Start a logo from a star or blob, then convert it to a path and refine it.

details.text: In the tool dock's Shapes menu, Design Tools → Insert, the Generators sheet and Insert → Blobs… on Mac. Eleven styles: Organic, Wobbly Circle, Splash, Cloud, Star Blob, Squiggle Ribbon, Pebble, Goo, Gradient Blob, Burst and Ring, each with its own controls.
Shared blob controls. Randomness scales every style's irregularity; Symmetry is None, Mirror or 2-, 3-, 4-, 5-, 6- or 8-Fold. Shuffle picks a new seed.
Insert 1–24 blobs at once in a Scatter, Row or Grid, with Spacing and Size Variance. Each blob gets its own seed. On the free plan the whole count must fit the item allowance.

In the Shapes menu, Design Tools → Insert and Insert → Stars… on Mac. Presets: Classic Star, Sparkle, Badge, Burst and Soft Star. Points run from 3 to 50, plus Inner Radius, Roundness, Rotation and Size.
Filled or Outlined (with Outline Width) and a color. Gradient Blob fills with one of its gradient presets.

Select an inserted blob or star to change its style, controls or seed in the inspector. Resizing, moving and duplicating keep working, and a resize sticks through later tweaks. Each slider drag is one undo step.
From the right-click menu or the inspector, for blobs, stars and other shapes. The result opens in point editing; fill, stroke and effects are kept, but the generator controls are removed.

tips: Use Symmetry for logo-like marks and leave it at None for natural shapes.
Lower Randomness for calmer shapes behind text.
Use Size Variance with Scatter so clusters don't look repeated.
Convert to Path only when you need to move individual points; you lose the generator controls.
Try the Soft Star preset for friendly badges and Burst for sale tags.

features.title: Pen and vector editing
features.summary: Draw Bézier paths, edit their points and handles, outline strokes and merge shapes.
steps: Choose the Pen tool. Click to add corner points, or drag to add smooth points. Click the first point to close the path.
Select a path and press Return to edit its points. Drag points and handles; double-click a point to switch corner and smooth.
Press ⌥⌘O to turn a stroke into a filled shape (Outline Stroke).
Choose Vector → Shape Builder on overlapping shapes, then drag across regions to merge them.

faq.q: Can I smooth a freehand line?
faq.a: Yes. Choose Convert to Smooth Path.

faq.q: How do I make a tapered stroke?
faq.a: Apply a Width Profile; it becomes an editable outline.

features.why: The Pen tool and path editing let you draw and refine any outline point by point, for custom icons, lettering and logos. Stroke tools turn lines into editable shapes when you need tapered or filled outlines.
uses: Trace a logo from a reference image.
Draw a custom icon with precise curves.
Turn a hand-drawn line into a smooth editable path.
Make a calligraphic swash with a tapered width profile.

details.text: Click to add corner points, drag to add smooth points, click the first point to close the path. Press Return to finish an open path.

Press Return with a path selected, or choose Vector › Edit Path. Drag points and handles, Shift-click to select several, double-click a point to switch corner and smooth, and click the path to add a point. Press Done to finish.
Corner, Mirrored or Asymmetric, from the Edit Path toolbar. On Mac, Option-drag a handle to break it from its partner.

details.term: Delete Point, Open Path and Close Path
details.text: Buttons in the Edit Path toolbar. A path needs at least three points to close.
Turns a stroke into a filled shape, keeping any fill.
Taper Both Ends, Taper End, Taper Start or Thick Middle. Bakes a variable-width stroke into an editable outline.
Turns freehand ink into a smooth path with editable points.

Vector › Shape Builder on 2 to 6 overlapping closed shapes. Drag across regions to Merge them, or switch to Delete to remove them. Clear resets; Apply replaces the shapes with the merged shape plus each remaining region, in one undo step.

tips: Use as few points as you can; smooth points with long handles give cleaner curves than many corner points.
Place points at the extremes of a curve (top, bottom, left, right) for easier editing.
Outline Stroke before you scale an icon if its line weight must scale with it.
Arrows don’t open in Edit Path, so their arrow settings are never lost. Convert them to a path first.

features.title: Boolean operations
features.summary: Combine closed shapes with Union, Subtract, Intersect and Exclude.
steps: Select two or more closed shapes in the same frame.
Choose Vector → Union, Subtract, Intersect or Exclude.
For an editable result, choose Vector → Live Boolean Group. Edit the original shapes any time.
Choose Flatten to turn a live group into one path.

faq.q: Which shape does Subtract keep?
faq.a: The bottom shape; the others are cut from it.

faq.q: Can I undo a boolean?
faq.a: Yes. One undo restores the original shapes.

features.why: Boolean operations build complex shapes from simple ones: cut holes, merge outlines, or keep only an overlap. Use a live boolean group when you may still adjust the parts.
uses: Cut a hole in a circle to make a ring.
Merge a rounded rectangle and a triangle into a speech bubble.
Keep only the overlap of two circles for a lens shape.
Build an icon from basic shapes and keep it editable.

details.text: Merges all the selected shapes into one outline.
Keeps the bottom shape and cuts the shapes above it out of it.
Keeps only the area where the shapes overlap.
Keeps everything except the overlap.
Two or more closed shapes on the same board layer and in the same frame. Rectangles, ovals, polygons, stars, closed pen paths and filled paths qualify; open lines and freehand ink don’t.
One path with the bottom shape’s fill and stroke. Holes stay open in export. Rectangle corner radii become fixed points. One undo restores the originals.

Vector › Live Boolean Group keeps the shapes as hidden layers and recomputes the result whenever they change. In the Boolean Group section, Show Shapes to Edit reveals them and Hide Shapes hides them again.
Turns a live boolean group into one fixed path.

tips: Use a live boolean group while a design is still changing, and flatten it when it’s final.
For Subtract, send the shape you want to keep to the back first.
Use Shape Builder when you want to keep some regions and remove others in one pass.

features.title: Editable arrows
features.summary: Draw arrows that stay editable: drag the ends, bend the curve, and change heads, tails and thickness.
steps: Choose the Arrow tool (A) from the Shapes menu or Pencil palette. Drag from tail to tip; Shift snaps to 45°.
Select the arrow. Drag the round end handles to move the ends, and the diamond handle to bend it.
In the Arrow inspector, choose Start and End heads (Triangle, Open, Swept or None) and tail caps.
Adjust Thickness, Taper, Head Size and Curve, or pick a preset such as Bold or Swoosh.
Style it like any shape with Fill, Stroke and Effects.

faq.q: Do arrows attach to other layers?
faq.a: No. Arrows are free-standing shapes, not connectors.

faq.q: How do I straighten a bent arrow?
faq.a: Choose Straighten in the inspector, or drag the midpoint close to the line; it snaps straight.

features.why: Arrows point at things on a board: callouts, flows, annotations and diagrams. Mica’s arrows are filled shapes that taper and bend, so they look drawn rather than mechanical and still take any fill or effect.
uses: Point at a detail in a reference image with a curved callout.
Show a flow between screens in a presentation.
Make a bold swoosh arrow for a poster or social post.
Draw a double-ended arrow to mark a measurement.

details.text: In the Shapes menu and the Pencil palette. Drag from tail to tip. Shift snaps to 45° and Option draws from the center. The arrow starts straight, is named Arrow and is selected.

Round handles at both ends and a diamond handle at the middle of the curve. Drag an end to move it; the bend keeps its shape. Drag the middle to bend; it snaps straight within 6 points. On Mac, Shift snaps ends to 45° and keeps the bend symmetric.
Standard, Bold, Swoosh, Double-Ended and Line. Presets keep the arrow’s ends.
Triangle, Open, Swept or None, separately for each end.
For an end without a head: Square, Round or Pointed.

details.term: Thickness, Taper, Head Size and Curve
details.text: Thickness from 0.5 to 400. Taper from 0 to 100 %, narrowing toward the tail. Head Size from 120 to 800 % of the thickness. Curve from −150 to 150 % of the length.
Straighten removes the bend. Reverse Direction swaps the ends and their heads.
Turns the arrow into a plain path with the same outline, for point editing. The arrow settings are gone after that.

tips: Resizing keeps thickness and head size, so resize first and then fine-tune Thickness.
Use Taper with a Swept head for a hand-drawn look.
Arrows don’t attach to other layers; move them with the layers they point at by grouping them.
Style arrows with gradients, outlines and shadows like any shape.

features.title: SVG and SF Symbols
features.summary: Paste or drop SVGs as editable layers, and insert SF Symbols as vector shapes.
steps: Copy as SVG in Figma or Illustrator, then paste in Mica. Or drop an .svg file onto the canvas.
Mica creates editable layers inside a frame sized to the SVG.
To add an icon, choose Design Tools → Insert → SF Symbol…, search, then set weight, color and size.
Choose a symbol to place it as a filled vector shape.

faq.q: Is every SVG feature supported?
faq.a: Paths, basic shapes, transforms, gradients and nested SVGs are. Scripts and animation are not.

faq.q: Can I recolor a symbol?
faq.a: Yes. It’s an ordinary shape, so change its fill.

features.why: SVG import brings vector artwork from Figma, Illustrator and icon sets into Mica as layers you can edit, not as flat images. SF Symbols give you Apple’s icon set as vector shapes for app mockups.
uses: Paste an icon copied as SVG from Figma and recolor it.
Drop an illustration .svg onto a board and edit its parts.
Add SF Symbols to an iOS app mockup.
Reuse a logo SVG at any size without blur.

details.text: Paste SVG (Copy as SVG in Figma or Illustrator), drop .svg files on the canvas, or insert them with the file picker. Mica creates editable layers inside a named, unfilled frame sized to the SVG, in one undo step.
Paths, rectangles, circles, ellipses, lines, polylines and polygons, transforms, nested SVGs, use and symbol, CSS classes and inline styles, linear and radial gradients, group opacity, and text.

Axis-aligned rectangles become editable rectangles with a corner radius. Gradients become gradient fills. Top-level groups become Mica groups. Text becomes Auto Width text in the named font when it’s installed.
Filters, clip paths, masks, patterns, embedded images and text on a path. Mica lists what it skipped in a notice. Scripts and animation aren’t imported.
Design Tools › Insert › SF Symbol…, also in Quick Actions. Search about 330 symbols and tap one to insert it.
Weight from Ultralight to Heavy (default Regular). Color with an eyedropper (default black). Size from 8 to 2048 points (default 96).
Symbols insert as filled vector shapes traced from a high-resolution render, so you can recolor, resize and combine them like any shape.

tips: Clean up SVGs in the source app first: expand strokes or remove clip paths if they don’t import as expected.
Each imported shape counts toward the free plan’s 12 items per board.
SF Symbols are licensed for designs of apps for Apple platforms.

features.title: Tables
features.summary: Insert a table or paste spreadsheet cells as a table built from Super Layout frames.
steps: Choose Design Tools → Insert → Table for a 4 × 3 table.
Or copy cells from a spreadsheet or CSV, then press ⌥⇧⌘V (Paste as Table).
Double-click a cell to edit its text.
Use the Table inspector to add or delete rows and columns.

faq.q: How big can a pasted table be?
faq.a: Up to 200 rows by 40 columns.

faq.q: Can I style cells?
faq.a: Yes. Cells are frames and text layers, so every style option applies.

features.why: Tables put structured data on a board: specs, comparisons, schedules or pasted spreadsheet ranges. Each cell is an ordinary frame with a text layer, so every style option applies.
uses: Paste a pricing comparison from Numbers or Excel.
Lay out a spec sheet next to product images.
Track a shot list or schedule on a moodboard.
Style a data table for a presentation slide.

details.text: Design Tools › Insert › Table, also in Quick Actions. Adds a 4-row, 3-column table at the center of the view.
Turns copied CSV, TSV or spreadsheet cells into a table. Quoted values are respected. Up to 200 rows and 40 columns.
The table is a Super Layout frame of rows, and each row holds cells with one text layer each. Cells are 140 points wide and 36 points tall to start.
The first row is the header, with semibold 14-point text on a light gray fill. Other cells use regular 14-point text.
In the Table section. Add a row below, or a column to the right of, the selected cell, or at the end.
Remove the row or column of the selected cell. They aren’t available with the whole table selected or when only one row or column is left.
Each cell uses two items (its frame and its text), plus one per row and one for the table. On the free plan this counts toward the 12 items per board.

tips: Double-click a cell to edit its text; cell text wraps at the cell width.
Select Same Type or Select Same Font to restyle every cell at once.
Use Publication Export when you need the data back as CSV or JSON.

features.title: Fill, stroke and color
features.summary: Stack solid, gradient, image and noise paints, and style strokes, all in the Fill & Stroke section.
steps: Select a frame, shape or text and open Fill & Stroke in Properties.
Click + to add a paint. Click its swatch to choose Solid, Linear, Radial, Angular, Diamond, Image or Noise.
In the color picker, drag the field or type a hex value; use the eyedropper or the board’s saved colors.
Set each paint’s opacity and blend mode, hide it with the eye, or drag rows to reorder.
Add a stroke and set its width, position, cap, join and dash.

faq.q: Which images can I use as an image fill?
faq.a: Images already on the board. The fill reuses the original; nothing is copied.

faq.q: How many paints can a layer have?
faq.a: Up to 16.

features.why: Fill & Stroke controls how a frame, shape or text layer is painted. Stacking several paints lets you combine gradients, textures and images in one layer instead of piling up extra layers.
uses: Give a button a gradient fill with a subtle noise paint on top.
Put a photo into a shape with an image fill.
Draw a card with a 1-point inside border on the top edge only.
Sample a color from a reference image with the eyedropper.

details.text: Solid, Linear, Radial, Angular, Diamond, Image or Noise. A layer can have up to 16 fill paints and 16 stroke paints.
Each row has a swatch, hex value, opacity, visibility and remove. Drag rows, or use Move Up and Move Down, to change the order.

Each paint blends with the paints below it using one of 16 modes: Normal, Darken, Multiply, Color Burn, Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity.

Drag stops on the gradient bar, click it to add a stop, and set each stop’s color, position and opacity. Reverse flips the stops. Angle runs from −360° to 360°. Edit Gradient on Canvas shows handles for start, end, width and stops.
Choose Image or Change Image to use an image already on the board; nothing is copied. Scale: Fill, Fit, Tile (with Tile % from 1 to 1000) or Stretch. Text doesn’t take image fills.
Amount % from 0 to 100 and Size from 0.25 to 32.
Stroke paints have a Width up to 1000 and a Position of Inside, Center or Outside. Frames can set a different width for each side. Shapes also have their own outline with cap, join and dash options.

Opens inline under the row. Saturation and brightness field, hue and opacity bars, Hex, RGB or HSB entry, the board’s saved colors, and an eyedropper that samples anywhere on screen (on Mac, even other apps).
With frames, closed shapes or text selected, press I to start the eyedropper; the sampled color becomes each layer’s top fill in one undo step.

tips: Hide a paint with its eye to compare versions without losing its settings.
Use Inside strokes on frames and cards so borders don’t change their size.
Add a low-opacity Noise paint over a gradient to reduce banding.
Save colors you reuse as color styles or variables so you can update them in one place.

features.title: Shadows, blurs, noise and texture
features.summary: Add drop and inner shadows, layer and background blur, noise and texture from the Effects section.
steps: Select a layer and click + in Effects.
Choose Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow, Layer Blur, Background Blur, Noise or Texture.
Click the effect row to open its settings, such as offset, blur, spread and color.
Hide an effect with the eye to keep its settings, or remove it.

faq.q: Why does my PNG cutout cast a shaped shadow?
faq.a: Shadows come from visible pixels, so transparent areas cast nothing.

faq.q: Where are the bigger effects?
faq.a: Open the Effect Studio for particles, lighting, outlines and more.

features.why: Effects add depth and texture without extra layers: shadows lift cards off the page, blurs create frosted glass, and noise and texture add grain. They stay editable and export with the layer.
uses: Lift a card with a soft drop shadow.
Make a pressed-in search field with an inner shadow.
Create a frosted glass panel over a photo with background blur.
Add film grain to a poster with noise.

details.text: Inner Shadow, Drop Shadow, Layer Blur, Background Blur, Noise or Texture. A layer can have one of each.

Color, opacity, X, Y, Blur and Spread. Starts black at 25 % with Y 4 and Blur 12. Offset and spread up to ±2,000, blur up to 500. Shadows come from the visible pixels, so transparent areas cast nothing. Works on every layer.
Frames and closed shapes. Same settings as a drop shadow, drawn inside the edge.
Grows the shadow’s shape before it’s blurred. A negative value shrinks it.
Blurs the layer itself, up to 250. Works on frames, shapes, text and notes.
Blurs what is below the layer inside its shape, up to 250. It shows through a translucent fill, so lower the fill opacity or use a gradient with transparent stops.
Mono, Duo or Multi, with Size, Density %, colors and Opacity %.
Size, Radius and Clip to Shape.
Each row has an eye that hides the effect and keeps its settings, and a remove button. Click the row to open its settings.

tips: Use low opacity (10–25 %) and a larger blur for natural shadows.
Shadows on PNG cutouts follow the cutout’s shape, not its box.
Save shadows and blurs you reuse as an effect style.
For particles, lighting and outlines, open the Effect Studio.

features.title: Blend modes and image adjustments
features.summary: Blend layers with the canvas below, and adjust images without changing the original file.
steps: Select a layer and choose a blend mode in Appearance.
Select an image and open Adjustments.
Drag Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Saturation, Temperature or Tint.
Reset any slider to return to the original.

faq.q: Are adjustments destructive?
faq.a: No. They apply per placement; the original stays untouched.

faq.q: Do adjustments work on video?
faq.a: No, only on still images.

features.why: Blend modes mix a layer with what is below it, for textures, light leaks and tinted overlays. Image adjustments correct exposure and color on a placed image without changing the original file.
uses: Lay a paper texture over a design with Multiply.
Brighten a dark reference photo with Exposure and Shadows.
Warm up a cool image with Temperature before comparing palettes.
Add glow over an image with Screen or Plus Lighter.

details.text: In Appearance: Normal, Multiply, Screen or Plus Lighter. These match exactly on the canvas and in PNG, PDF and SVG export.
For more modes, such as Overlay or Soft Light, set the blend mode on a paint in Fill & Stroke; it blends with the paints below it in the same layer.
From −3 to 3.
Each from −1 to 1.
Each from −1 to 1, to warm, cool or shift the white balance.
Double-click a value to reset that slider, or choose Reset Adjustments to reset them all. Each slider gesture is one undo step.
Adjustments apply per placement, so two copies of one image can look different. They don’t apply to video, board covers or publication exports.

tips: Multiply darkens and drops white; Screen lightens and drops black. Choose by which one you want to disappear.
Adjust a duplicate of a reference to compare before and after side by side.
Drag a slider’s label to scrub its value precisely.

features.title: Erase parts of a layer
features.summary: Erase and restore parts of an image without changing the original.
steps: Select an image and choose Erase… from the right-click menu or the inspector’s actions.
Choose Erase and drag over the parts to remove. Set Size and Hardness, or press [ and ] to resize the brush.
Choose Restore to paint parts back, or Restore All to start over. Turn on Show Erased to see what you removed.
Choose Apply to keep the result, or Cancel to discard it.

faq.q: Is the original image changed?
faq.a: No. The erase is stored as a mask, so you can paint areas back later.

faq.q: Does it work after Remove Background?
faq.a: Yes. Erase… refines the same mask that Remove Background makes.

faq.q: Which layers can I erase?
faq.a: Still images whose file is on this device.

features.why: Sometimes Remove Background gets close but not all the way, or you need to cut part of a reference out. The layer eraser lets you brush pixels away and back without touching the original image.
uses: Clean up the edges after Remove Background.
Cut a figure out of a photo for a collage.
Fade out part of a reference with a soft brush.
Restore an area that was removed by mistake.

details.text: In the canvas right-click menu and the inspector's actions, for still images whose file is on this device (the same images Remove Background works on).
Two brushes: Erase removes pixels, Restore paints them back.
Size runs from 2 to 300 pt; press [ and ] to change it. Hardness goes from soft to crisp. A circle cursor shows the brush.
Show Erased draws removed pixels faintly. Restore All brings everything back.
⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z undo and redo up to 24 steps while the studio is open. Cancel discards everything; Apply writes one canvas undo step.

The erase is saved as the image's mask, shared with Remove Background, at up to 2,048 px. The source image is never changed, and the mask travels with exports, .refboard files and duplicates. Applying a fully restored mask removes it.

tips: Run Remove Background first, then refine its edges with Erase….
Use a soft brush for hair and fur, and a hard brush for product edges.
Turn on Show Erased to check you haven't removed too much.
Use Restore rather than Undo to bring back a small area.

features.title: Color, text, effect and grid styles
features.summary: Save reusable styles, apply them anywhere on the board, and update every linked layer at once.
steps: Style a layer the way you want, then choose Create Style in its style section.
Select other layers and apply the style from the styles list.
Change the original, then choose Update Style to update every linked layer.
Use the Pick Text Style eyedropper to copy a text style from another layer. Detach a layer to unlink it.

faq.q: What does “(modified)” mean?
faq.a: The layer is linked to a style but has local changes.

faq.q: Can I recolor everything that uses a color?
faq.a: Yes. Selection Colors in the inspector lists every color in the selection; edit one to recolor every use.

features.why: Styles store a color, text look, effect set or layout grid under a name. Layers linked to a style update together, so a brand color or heading change is one edit instead of dozens.
uses: Keep brand colors consistent across every page of a board.
Change the heading font on all screens at once.
Reuse the same card shadow on many components.
Share styles with other boards through a library.

details.text: Save Color Style, Save Text Style, Save Effect Style and Save Grid Style create a style from the selected layer. The list shows each style with its linked item count.
Frame, sticky and palette colors.
Whole-layer font family, size, weight, italic, alignment and color. Applying one replaces mixed formatting; undo restores it.
Effect styles save shadows, blurs and blend mode. Grid styles save a frame’s layout grids.
Pushes the selected layer’s look to the style and every linked layer on the board. Locked or private items block the update.
A layer with local changes shows its style name with (modified). Changing a linked value by hand detaches that layer and keeps its look. Detach Styles unlinks the selection.

With text or sticky layers selected, tap another text layer to copy its family, size, weight, italic, alignment, color and spacing onto the selection in one undo step. Esc or tapping empty canvas cancels.
Lists every color in the selection with use counts. Edit one to recolor every use, or choose Create Color Style…, Create Color Variable… or Select Layers Using This Color.
Rename and delete styles; deleted styles leave layers with their current look. Libraries publishes this board’s styles and variables for other boards to use.

tips: Create styles early, as soon as a color or text look repeats.
Filter the Layers panel by No Style to find layers that should use a style.
Use Selection Colors to turn hard-coded colors into a style in one step.

features.title: Copy properties and Select Same
features.summary: Copy one layer’s look onto others, and select every layer that matches.
steps: Select the layer whose look you want and press ⌥⌘C (Copy Properties).
Select the target layers and press ⌥⌘V (Paste Properties).
To select similar layers, choose Design Tools → Select Same, then pick type, source, fill, stroke, font, size, effect or style.

faq.q: What gets copied?
faq.a: Opacity, effects, fill, stroke and typography, including the font family.

faq.q: Does Select Same include hidden layers?
faq.a: No. Only visible, unlocked layers are selected.

features.why: Copying properties matches one layer’s look on others without restyling them by hand. Select Same finds every layer that shares a property, so you can change them together.
uses: Give new buttons the same fill, stroke and shadow as an existing one.
Copy only the drop shadow from one card to several others.
Select every layer with the same fill and recolor them.
Find every text layer in one font size and change it.

details.text: Copies opacity, effects, fill, stroke and typography, including the font family and spacing.

With one layer selected, opens a checklist of what the layer has: Transform (Size, Rotation, Flip), Appearance (Opacity, Blend Mode, Fill, Stroke, Corner Radius), Effects, Text and Image. Use Select All or Select None, then Copy. The sheet remembers your choices.

Applies the copied properties to every selected editable layer in one undo step: everything after ⌥⌘C, only the checked attributes after ⇧⌘C. Each layer takes what applies to it. Paste in Place is ⌃⌘V.
Pasting detaches linked color and text styles on the targets, since they now use local values.

Design Tools › Select Same: Type, Source, Fill, Stroke, Font, Size, Effect or Style. Fill compares hex values; Font compares the face and size of the first character; Size compares width and height rounded to whole points.
Adds every layer of the same kind and name, with the same parent and nesting depth.
Select Same and Select Matching Layers pick only visible, unlocked layers on the current page.

tips: Copied properties stay available across boards until you copy again.
Use Copy Attributes… when you want the shadow but not the fill, or the size but not the color.
Combine Select Same with Paste Properties to restyle a whole set in two steps.
If you want the link to stay, apply a style instead of pasting properties.

features.title: Use the Effect Studio
features.summary: A large studio for stacking effects on a layer: try them, tune them, then apply them in one undoable step.
steps: Select a layer and open the Effect Studio from Properties, or from the Effects tab in the left rail.
Choose an effect in the grid to preview it. Its settings open right away.
Tune it with the sliders and colors, then choose Add to Stack.
Drag rows in the stack to reorder; the top row draws on top. Hide or remove rows as needed.
Choose Apply to keep the result, or Cancel to discard it.

faq.q: Do effects slow the board down?
faq.a: Each effect is baked once, so a finished stack costs about as much as an image.

faq.q: Are studio effects animated?
faq.a: No. They are static looks.

features.why: Some looks need more than a drop shadow: glows, particles, haze, outlines and light that sit on top of a layer. The Effect Studio gives you a large preview where you can try those effects, tune them and stack several before anything touches the board. Use it when you want to try a few ideas, then keep only the one that works.
uses: Add Dreamy Bokeh and a soft Vignette to a product photo for a moodboard cover.
Turn a vector logo into a Neon Tube sign with a halo that reaches past the shape.
Paint Ground Fog under a subject by hand, only where you want it.
Stack a Lens Flare, Film Grain and a lighting look on a hero image, then reorder them until the result looks right.

details.text: In the Effect Studio section of Properties, or by choosing an effect in the Effects tab of the left rail. Works on images, files, links, stickies, text, vector drawings, palettes and frames.

On iPhone and iPad the studio fills the screen. On Mac it is a sheet nearly the size of the window, at least 860 × 620 points, that follows the window as it resizes. From 860 points wide it uses two columns: a large preview and a controls column with the stack on top and Browse and Settings below. On a narrow iPhone you switch between Effects, Browse and Settings. Vision Pro uses a sheet.

The effect grid, grouped by type, with a Search Effects field. Choosing a card previews that effect without adding it. Outline effects and Glitch Split are shown on a sample star, so you can see what they do to a shape.
Keeps the effect you are trying. Until then it is a trial: switching to another effect keeps what you tuned on each one for the session, and Cancel never asks about a trial you didn't add.

The stack. The top row draws on top. Drag rows to reorder (on touch, drag by the grip; on Mac, drag the whole row), use the eye to hide a row, and minus to remove it. Move Up and Move Down are also in each row's context menu.
Every effect has an Opacity slider from 0 to 100% and a Blend Mode. If a brightening blend mode would vanish over a light or transparent layer, the studio says so and offers Use Normal.
Keeps the effect inside the layer's bounds. On by default, except for outline effects such as Neon Tube and Long Shadow, which start unclipped so they can reach past the layer.

Covers only the layer's content, not its transparent areas. Edge Threshold (0 to 95%) sets how opaque a pixel must be to count. On by default for lighting, flow, liquid and finishing effects, so a cutout only gets them where it has content.
Picks a new random arrangement for the effect, for example a different scatter of particles, while keeping every setting.
Effects with colors list them under Colors. Use Add Color to add one and minus to remove one.

Zoom controls in the preview's bottom-right corner: zoom out, a percentage that fits the layer again when you tap it, and zoom in. Pinch, or press ⌘−, ⌘0 and ⌘=. Zoom runs from 20% to 800%, dragging empty space pans, and a thin outline marks the layer's edge. Past 125% and 175% the preview re-renders with more detail.
Apply bakes exactly what the preview shows, including an effect still on trial, as one undoable edit named Effect Studio. Cancel discards the session and leaves the layer as it was.

After you apply, the Effect Studio section in Properties lists the stack. You can reorder, hide, remove and toggle Clip to Visible Pixels there without reopening the studio. Layers with studio effects show a small count badge on their icon in the Layers panel.

Each effect is baked once into a cached texture. It stretches while you resize the layer and rebakes after, so a finished stack costs about as much as an image. Effects follow the layer's opacity and hide at zero. Effects that need re-rendering in the studio draw side by side, so an edited stack updates quickly. Zooming never changes where an effect renders.

tips: Try several effects before you add any. The studio remembers what you tuned on each one until you close it.
Put broad effects such as haze and lighting low in the stack and finishing touches such as Film Grain or Vignette at the top.
If an effect spills onto a transparent background, turn on Clip to Visible Pixels and raise Edge Threshold until the edge is clean.
Use Shuffle when particles land in an awkward spot, instead of nudging Center X and Y.
Effects are part of the layer, so they come along when you duplicate the layer, export a .refboard or undo.

features.title: Studio effects library
features.summary: 59 effects: particles, light, flow, liquid and atmosphere, finishing, outlines and cutouts, and pop and retro looks.
steps: Open the Effect Studio and browse the groups in the effect grid.
Particle effects expose occurrence, size, randomness and spread.
For flares, rays and Comic Burst, tap the preview to place them, as many times as you like.
Outline effects such as Neon Tube, Die-Cut Sticker and Long Shadow follow the layer’s shape and can reach past it.

faq.q: Can effects pixelate my image?
faq.a: No. Studio effects paint over a layer and never read its pixels.

faq.q: Which layers get a custom outline?
faq.a: Filled vector shapes. Images and text use their box as the outline.

features.why: The library gives you finished looks that would otherwise need a separate graphics app: particles, light rays, fog, liquid patterns, outlines and retro textures. Every setting is a slider or a color, so you can push an effect from subtle to bold without leaving the board.
uses: Scatter Confetti or Glitter over a party invitation and tune how many pieces appear.
Place two or three Lens Flares on a night photo by tapping the preview.
Give a vector badge a Die-Cut Sticker border and a Long Shadow.
Make a quick poster background from Liquid Metal, Nebula or Retro Sunset on an empty frame.

details.text: Floating Particles, Fireflies, Dreamy Bokeh, Star Shimmer, Star Shower, Confetti, Snowfall, Rainfall, Embers, Bubbles, Glitter and Dust Motes. Occurrence sets how many (1 to 1,500), with Size, Size Randomness, Opacity Randomness, Center X and Y, Spread from Center, Position Randomness, Depth of Field and Focus Distance. Some add their own control, such as Aperture Blades, Thin-Film Color or Tumble.

Anima Radiance, Lens Flare, Light Leak, Starburst, Halo Ring and Prism Beam. Each has Center X and Y, Size, Intensity and Softness, plus optics such as Rays, Ghosts, Anamorphic Streak, Aperture Blades, Chromatic Fringe, Dispersion and Glow. Tap the preview to place a source, then another; drag to move them. They are listed under Placed Sources.

Haze, Mist, Ground Fog, Smoke Wisps, Light Shafts and Drifting Dust, with Density, Coverage, Softness, Scale, Turbulence, Detail and Drift Direction. Turn on Paint by Hand to brush them in: choose Paint or Erase and set Brush Size, Brush Softness and Brush Strength. Clear and Fill reset the painted area.

Neon Tube, Die-Cut Sticker, Long Shadow, Ink Sketch, Stitched Edge, Marquee Bulbs and Glass Bevel. They trace the layer's outline and start unclipped so they can reach past it. Filled vector shapes give their own outline; images and text use their box.
Holographic Foil, Retro Sunset, Glitch Split, Stained Glass, Pixel Dither, CRT Screen, Speed Lines and Comic Burst. Comic Burst can be placed several times by tapping the preview.
Silk Waves, Ribbon Flow, Ripple Rings, Topography and Moiré: line patterns with Lines, Amplitude, Thickness and Angle.
Aurora Glow, Liquid Shader, Liquid Metal, Fractal Sky, Plasma, Smoke, Marble, Iridescence, Caustics and Nebula: full-layer color fields.
Film Grain, Halftone, Scanlines, Vignette and Glass Sheen.

In its own Aurora group. Choosing it opens the studio waiting for a path: drag on the preview to draw where the aurora rises, and it renders when the stroke ends. A tap or very short stroke is ignored. The path can extend well past the layer, but the light stays inside the layer while Clip to Layer is on, the default. Drag path points to reshape the curve; Redraw Path starts over.

Studio effects paint over a layer and never read its pixels. That is why they work on transparent layers, and why there is no true pixelation, RGB split of the image itself, refraction or gradient map.
Effects don't animate. Particles, flares and fog are a single still frame.

1 to 6 Waves (3 by default) stand one behind another, set by Wave Spacing, Perspective, Depth Fade, Depth Blur and Front Wave Cover. The curtain itself has Curtain Height, Hem Brightness, Fade at Ends, Waviness, Folds, Rays, Ray Density, Rise Direction (also a turn handle on the preview) and Color Shift with Height. Horizontal Glow, Vertical Glow and Bloom spread the light into the air.

Up to 12 color stops along the path. Drag a color from the tray on the preview, which includes the board's color styles, onto the path to add a stop there. Slide stops along the path, or drag one well off the path to remove it. Settings list every stop, with Add Color and Reverse.

tips: For outline effects, use a filled vector shape when you want the effect to follow a custom silhouette. On images and text they follow the box.
Raise Depth of Field on particle effects to blur the near and far pieces for a photographic look.
Pixel Dither, CRT Screen, Halftone and Scanlines can show a faint moiré on the canvas when zoomed out. Zoom in or check the export, which is unaffected.
Lower the Opacity of a busy effect, such as Glitter, before you reduce Occurrence. It often keeps the texture while calming it down.
Atmosphere effects look most natural when painted by hand into the areas where fog or haze would really gather.
For Aurora Pen, draw the path along the horizon of your image and raise Bloom slightly for a glow that spills into the sky.

features.title: Studio lighting
features.summary: Add lights to a layer and aim them on a small 3D stage.
steps: In the Effect Studio, add a light or choose a lighting look.
Drag the light on the stage to move it in X and Y; lift it for Z and drag to aim.
Set intensity, reach, softness, cone and how much the surroundings darken.
Choose a circular light or one that matches the layer’s shape.

faq.q: Can I use several lights?
faq.a: Yes. Lights stack like any other effect.

faq.q: Do lights affect other layers?
faq.a: No. Each light belongs to the layer you added it to.

features.why: Flat artwork and photos often look pasted on. Studio lighting adds a light you can place and aim around the layer, with falloff, cone and darkened surroundings, so you can direct attention or match the light of a scene.
uses: Spotlight a product on a dark background and let the edges fall into shadow.
Warm up a portrait with Warm Glow coming from one side.
Add a cool rim of Edge Light to a cutout so it separates from the background.
Combine two lights of different colors for a stage-lit look.

details.text: Even Wash, Soft Glow, Hard Spot, Spotlight, Warm Glow and Cool Focus, in the Lighting group of the effect grid. Each is a starting point; every value can be changed.
A small 3D view of the light around the layer. Drag the ring on the plane to move the light in X and Y, drag the sphere to lift it in Z, and drag the crosshair to aim it.
X and Y (−50 to 150%, so a light can sit outside the layer), Z (Height) from 5 to 200%, Intensity from 0 to 300%, Color Temperature from 1,500 to 12,000 (6,500 by default) and Source Size.
Aim X and Aim Y, Cone Angle from 5° to 90°, Softness, Reach and Falloff.
Surface Sheen, Glossiness and Edge Light shape how the layer's surface catches the light.
Haze adds a visible glow in the air. Darken Surroundings dims everything the light doesn't reach.
Off by default, so the light is circular. Turn it on to shape the light like the layer.
Lights are effects in the stack, so you can add several, reorder them and hide or remove each one. Each belongs only to the layer you added it to.

tips: Start from a lighting look close to what you want, then fine-tune on the stage rather than from scratch.
Raise Darken Surroundings for drama, and keep it low when the layer needs to stay readable.
Lower Z and widen Reach for a grazing light that brings out texture.
Use Color Temperature instead of a colored layer to warm or cool a photo; it keeps the light natural.

features.title: Super Layout
features.summary: Arrange a frame’s children in a row, column or wrapped rows with exact gaps and padding. Everything reflows when content changes.
steps: Select a frame or several layers and press ⇧A (Add Super Layout). Mica reads direction, gap and padding from the arrangement.
In the Super Layout section, choose the flow: Vertical, Horizontal, Wrap or Grid.
Set the gap and padding, and place the content with the 9-point alignment matrix.
Under Spacing, choose Packed, Space Between, Space Around or Space Evenly.
Press ⌥⇧A to remove Super Layout.

faq.q: Can children overlap?
faq.a: Yes. Use a negative gap, or set a child to Absolute Position.

faq.q: Can I align text on its baseline?
faq.a: Yes, in horizontal flows.

faq.q: How do I change the defaults for new layouts?
faq.a: Settings → Canvas → New Super Layout.

features.why: Placing buttons, cards and lists by hand means re-spacing everything whenever content changes. Super Layout makes a frame arrange its children for you with exact gaps and padding, and reflows them when you add, remove or resize something. Reach for it for anything that repeats or grows: toolbars, lists, cards, tags and slides.
uses: Build a button whose frame grows with its label, with fixed padding on every side.
Make a vertical list of cards that stays evenly spaced as you add or delete cards.
Lay out a row of tags that wraps onto new lines when it runs out of width.
Distribute a toolbar's icons with Space Between so they fill the bar.

details.text: Works on a frame or on several sibling layers. Mica reads the direction, gaps, padding and alignment from the current arrangement, including grids and wrapped rows, so nothing moves. Remove Super Layout is ⌥⇧A, or the button at the bottom of the section.
Vertical, Horizontal, Wrap or Grid. Wrap needs a fixed width (or height, for vertical flows) to break lines.
A 9-point matrix places the content in the frame. With an Auto spacing choice, the spread axis shows as a line and only the other axis takes a choice.
Gap accepts negative values to overlap children, up to ±4,096. Spacing is Fixed Gap, Auto: Space Between, Auto: Space Around or Auto: Space Evenly.
For Wrap and Grid flows. Auto spreads the lines across a fixed counter axis instead.
Top, Right, Bottom and Left are set separately.
Fixed Width or Hug Width, and Fixed Height or Hug Height, for the frame. A hugging frame shows Min & Max Size fields.
A toggle on a child. The child stays where you put it and takes no space in the flow. Hidden children also take no space.

Strokes: Excluded (default) or Included, so a frame's stroke insets its content and children's outer strokes count toward their size. Canvas Stacking: Last on Top (default) or First on Top. Align Text Baselines, for horizontal flows.
Settings → Canvas → New Super Layout. Infer from Arrangement is on by default. Turn it off to always start from a saved Direction, Gap and Padding, and choose whether new layouts use First on Top.

tips: Arrange layers roughly first, then press ⇧A. The inferred gap and padding usually need no correction.
Nest layouts: a horizontal row of vertical cards keeps both levels tidy, and hug sizes pass up through the nesting.
Use First on Top when the first child should overlap the next, such as stacked avatars with a negative gap.
Every change and its reflow is one undo step, so you can experiment freely.

hero.alt: A UI design workspace in Mica on Mac with layers, canvas and inspector

features.title: Grid flow
features.summary: Lay out children in columns and rows. Tracks can be auto, a fixed size or a share such as 1fr.
steps: Select a Super Layout frame and choose Grid as the flow.
Set the columns and rows: auto, a number, or a share such as 1fr.
Children fill cells in reading order; new rows appear as needed.
Select a child to give it a fixed cell, a span, or its own alignment in the cell.

faq.q: What happens when I drag a grid child?
faq.a: It moves to the cell you drop it in and loses its fixed cell.

faq.q: Can a child span two columns?
faq.a: Yes. Set its span in the child’s Super Layout Resizing section.

features.why: Rows and columns are not enough for galleries, dashboards and pricing tables. Grid flow lays children out on real tracks, so items line up in both directions, and you can let one child span several cells.
uses: Lay out a photo gallery in three equal 1fr columns.
Build a dashboard where a chart spans two columns and smaller stats fill the rest.
Make a pricing table with a fixed-width label column and flexible plan columns.
Create a calendar-style grid where new rows appear as you add days.

details.text: A stepper sets how many columns there are.

Type sizes separated by spaces: auto (as long as the content), a number in canvas units, or a share such as 1fr or 2fr of the space left over. Rows you don't list are auto, and rows appear as children need them. Up to 64 tracks each way.
The space between rows; Gap sets the space between columns. Auto spreads rows across a fixed height.
Grid columns accept Fixed Gap, Auto: Space Between, Auto: Space Around and Auto: Space Evenly.
On a child: Column and Row give it a fixed cell, counted from 1. Leave them empty to auto-place in reading order.
Cols and Rows on a child set how many tracks it covers.
Horizontal (Default, Left, Center, Right) and Vertical (Default, Top, Middle, Bottom) align a child inside its cell.

tips: Use 1fr columns for even galleries and mix a fixed number with 1fr when one column must stay a set width.
Give only the special items a fixed cell or span, and let the rest auto-place.
Dragging a grid child to a new cell clears its fixed cell, so set it again if it must stay put.
Add Super Layout reads an existing grid-like arrangement, so you can sketch a grid by hand and convert it.

features.title: Hug, Fill and min/max
features.summary: Let a frame hug its content, let children fill the space, and set limits.
steps: Select a Super Layout frame and set its width or height to Hug to wrap its children plus padding.
Select a child and set it to Fill to take the remaining space, or Fixed to keep its size.
Enter Min and Max sizes to limit how far a layer grows or shrinks.
Dragging a hugging side or a Fill child’s size switches it to Fixed.

faq.q: Which wins, min or max?
faq.a: Min, as in Figma.

faq.q: Does a hugging frame move when it resizes?
faq.a: No. Its top-left corner stays put.

features.why: A layout is only useful if its sizes respond: a button should grow with its label, and a search field should take whatever space is left. Hug, Fill and Min & Max Size describe that intent so frames resize correctly when content changes.
uses: Make a button hug its label so longer translations don't overflow.
Let a search field Fill the toolbar while the icons around it stay fixed.
Keep a card between 240 and 360 points wide with Min W and Max W.
Make every card in a column match the widest one with Fill across a hug frame.

details.text: On a Super Layout frame: the frame wraps its children plus padding. Its top-left corner stays put when it resizes.
On a child in a flow: it takes the remaining space. Along the flow it needs a fixed-size frame; across a hug frame it matches the largest child.
Fixed Width and Fixed Height keep the size you set.
Min W, Max W, Min H and Max H on any child in a flow and on hugging frames. Leave a field empty for no limit. When they conflict, Min wins, as in Figma.
Space that a Max refuses goes to the other Fill children. On wrapped lines, a Fill child breaks at its Min and then stretches. A Fill child that is itself a hug frame fills.
Dragging a hugging side, or a Fill child's size, switches it to Fixed, in the same undo step as the drag. Layouts reflow live while you drag a frame handle.

tips: Pair Fill with Min and Max so flexible items never shrink to nothing or stretch too far.
If Fill seems to do nothing, check that the parent is fixed along that direction, not hugging.
Sizing modes and min and max sizes can be bound to variables, so a mode switch can change a layout's behavior.
Wrap needs a fixed width to break lines; set the frame to Fixed Width before choosing Wrap.

features.title: Edit layouts on the canvas
features.summary: Drag padding and gaps directly, and reorder children with the insertion line.
steps: Select a Super Layout frame. Padding and gap bands, and dashed grid tracks, appear.
Drag a pink handle to change padding, gap or row gap.
Drag a child; a line shows where it will land, including in another row.
Or press the arrow keys to move a selected child through the flow.

faq.q: Why don’t I see the handles?
faq.a: They hide while dragging, on component instances, and when the frame is small on screen.

faq.q: Does this work with touch?
faq.a: Yes, on Mac, iPad, iPhone and Vision Pro.

features.why: Typing padding and gap values is precise but slow when you are still exploring. On-canvas handles let you drag spacing and reorder children directly, with the same results as the inspector.
uses: Widen a card's padding by dragging until it looks balanced.
Drag the gap between list items to tighten a list.
Move a tag to the next wrapped row by dragging it to the insertion line.
Step a selected item earlier or later in a toolbar with the arrow keys.

details.text: A selected Super Layout frame shows its padding and gaps as bands, and grid tracks as dashed lines.
Drag to change padding, gap or row gap. Each drag is one undo step.
While you drag a child, a line shows where it will land in the flow, including on another wrapped row or grid row.
Move a selected child through the flow, one position per press.
During drags, on component instances, and when the frame is small on screen. Zoom in to bring them back.
Mac, iPad, iPhone and Vision Pro, with pointer or touch.

tips: Drag handles to find the right spacing by eye, then round the value in the inspector.
Edit layout spacing on the main component; instances don't show handles.
Dragging a grid child into a new cell clears its fixed cell.

features.title: Tidy Up and Auto Organize
features.summary: Clean up loose layers in one step, or arrange a set as a grid, masonry, rows or a compact pack.
steps: Select loose layers and press ⌃⌥T (Tidy Up). They snap into the rows and columns they suggest, with even gaps.
For a full rearrange, choose Design Tools → Super Layout → Auto Organize.
Choose Grid, Masonry Columns, Rows or Compact Pack, and the sort order: position, name, type, color, size or date.
Set the gap and column count. Ghosts preview the result; choose Organize to apply.

faq.q: Does Tidy Up resize layers?
faq.a: No. Sizes and the selection’s top-left corner stay the same.

faq.q: Can I organize a frame’s contents?
faq.a: Yes, for a frame without Super Layout. Groups stay rigid and locked layers stay put.

features.why: Boards fill up with layers dropped anywhere. Tidy Up straightens a nearly aligned set in one step, and Auto Organize rearranges a whole set by a rule, without turning it into a Super Layout frame.
uses: Straighten a roughly placed grid of screenshots so rows and columns line up with even gaps.
Pack a pile of reference images into Masonry Columns, sorted by color.
Sort a set of icons by name into a neat grid.
Arrange the loose contents of a frame into rows, largest first.

details.text: Snaps loose layers onto the rows and columns they already suggest, with even gaps. Sizes and the selection's top-left corner stay the same. A second run moves nothing. Also in the Super Layout section as Tidy Up Contents.
Under Design Tools → Super Layout, in the selection's context menu, and in the Super Layout section of the inspector.
Grid, Masonry Columns, Rows or Compact Pack.
Current Position, Name, Type, Color, Largest First or Date Added.
Gap defaults to 24. Columns appears for Grid and Masonry Columns; leave it on Auto to let Mica choose.
Ghosts show the result while the panel is open. Organize N Layers applies it as one undo step.

A selection, or a plain frame's contents. Layers keep their size and move as a block from the selection's top-left corner. Complete groups move as one; locked layers and children of a Super Layout stay put.

tips: Use Tidy Up when the layout is nearly right, and Auto Organize when you want a different arrangement.
Sort by Color for moodboards: similar tones end up next to each other.
Group layers that belong together before organizing, so they stay together.
If the result should keep reflowing as content changes, use Super Layout instead.

features.title: Create a mirror layer
features.summary: A mirror shows another layer’s live content. Edit the source once and every mirror updates.
steps: Select one layer, frame or group.
Right-click and choose Create Mirror. The mirror appears to the right, named “Mirror of …”.
Move, resize, rotate or fade the mirror like any layer.
In the inspector, choose Scale to Fit or Original Size to control how the source fits.

faq.q: Can the source be on another page?
faq.a: Yes. Any layer on the same board works, even a hidden one.

faq.q: What if I delete the source?
faq.a: The mirror keeps its link and shows a faint placeholder. Undo brings the content back, or choose another source.

faq.q: Can I edit inside a mirror?
faq.a: No. Clicking it selects the mirror. Edit the source, or inline the mirror’s contents.

features.why: When the same artwork appears in several places, copies drift apart as you edit. A mirror shows another layer's live content, so you edit once and every mirror updates. Use it for repeated logos, a header shown on several slides, or a design shown at several sizes.
uses: Show the same app screen in a phone mockup and in a zoomed detail view.
Repeat a footer on every page of a presentation board.
Park master artwork on a hidden page and mirror it wherever it's needed.
Preview a logo at small and large sizes side by side while you refine it.

details.text: In the selection's context menu, the selection bar's menu and the canvas bar. Works on one selected layer, frame (with its contents) or whole group. The mirror appears 40 points to the right of the source, at the same size, named "Mirror of …". Undoable.
Scale to Fit scales the source uniformly to fit the mirror, centered. Original Size shows it 1:1, centered and clipped to the mirror.
Fills, text, ink, effects, masks and group opacity. Shadows, blur, stroke widths and dashes scale with the mirror. The mirror's own rotation and opacity apply on top.

Any layer on any page of the same board, including a hidden one. Hidden layers inside the source stay hidden. A source on a locked private page or layer shows nothing until it's unlocked, and is left out of exports.
Chains work up to four levels. A mirror can't point at itself, and mirrors that loop back show nothing.
Image, PDF, layer, screenshot and prototype exports draw mirrors like any layer. Duplicating, importing and copying keep the link, remapped to a copied source when the source comes along.
A new mirror counts toward the free plan's layer limit.

tips: Keep masters on a separate, hidden page so they're easy to find and can't be moved by accident.
Use Original Size when the mirror should crop the source, and Scale to Fit for thumbnails.
Clicking a mirror selects the mirror itself; to change the content, use Go to Source.
Mirrors draw their source live, so prefer them to duplicates whenever the content should stay identical.

features.title: Manage mirrors
features.summary: Change a mirror’s source, swap a layer with a mirror, turn a mirror back into layers, and find every mirror of a source.
steps: Select a mirror. In the inspector, use Change Source to pick another layer, or Go to Source to jump to it.
Right-click a layer and choose Swap with Mirror: a mirror takes its place and the real layer moves aside for editing.
Choose Inline Mirror Contents to replace a mirror with an editable copy in the same place.
Click the “N mirrors” capsule above a source to list its mirrors and jump to one.

faq.q: Why did Mica warn me when deleting a layer?
faq.a: Mirrors use it. Mica asks before deleting a source so mirrors don’t go blank by surprise.

faq.q: Can a mirror show another mirror?
faq.a: Yes, up to four levels. Loops show nothing.

features.why: Once mirrors are spread across a board, you need to find them, repoint them and sometimes turn them back into real layers. These tools keep mirrors manageable without hunting through pages.
uses: Swap a layer inside a slide with a mirror, then edit the real layer elsewhere.
Point every mirror of an old logo at the new logo in one step.
Turn a mirror into editable layers when one copy needs to differ.
Find every place a component sheet is mirrored before deleting it.

details.text: Shows the source's name, and its page when it's elsewhere. Change Source picks another layer; when a mirror shows nothing it reads Reconnect Mirror. Go to Source sits beside it and selects the source, switching page and zooming to it. Both are also in the canvas and Layers panel context menus.

On a layer or group. A mirror takes its exact place, rotation, frame, group and stacking slot. The real layers move 80 points to the right, out of the frame, and are selected for editing. One undo step. Not offered for mirrors, layers inside instances or locked layers.
Replaces a mirror with an editable copy in the same place, scale, rotation, frame and group, as one undo step. In the canvas context menu, the Layers panel and the inspector.

A small "N mirrors" capsule above a source counts its mirrors anywhere on the board. Click it to list them and jump to one; it switches page if needed. Hidden while presenting and when the layer is under 24 points on screen.

From the capsule or a source's context menu. Select the new source on the canvas or in the Layers panel, then confirm with Change Mirrors. Every mirror of the old source moves to the new one, keeping its size and fit, as one undo step. Esc cancels.
From the capsule or a source's context menu. After confirmation, deletes every editable mirror of the source on all pages; the source stays.
Deleting a layer that mirrors use asks first: "Used by N mirror layers", with Delete and Cancel. Deleting mirrors themselves doesn't ask.

Offers Pick on Canvas (a banner asks you to select the new source; Cancel or Esc stops), Same Source as Another Mirror (shown as "mirror → source"), and every frame, group and top-level layer, by page. Sources that would loop back are refused. Each change is one undo step, and undo also restores a changed fit.

A mirror whose source is missing, unset, hidden or loops back draws an orange placeholder with a capsule: Source Missing, No Source, Source Hidden or Mirror Loop. Its menu reconnects the mirror or selects it. In the Layers panel the mirror's icon gets an orange warning mark.
Studio effects that clip to the source's visible pixels, such as Soft Glow, draw in mirrors and in exported mirrors like they do on the source.

tips: Swap with Mirror, edit, then Inline Mirror Contents to move a layer out of a frame and back in one round trip.
Check the mirrors capsule before restyling a source; the change shows everywhere.
Use Change Mirrored Source… instead of reconnecting mirrors one by one.
Mirror rows in the Layers panel use a flip icon, so you can spot them at a glance.

features.title: Components and instances
features.summary: Turn a frame into a main component and place linked instances. Edit the main once to update every instance.
steps: Select a frame and press ⌥⌘K (Create Component).
Choose Create Instance to place a linked copy, on this or another page.
Change text, fills or images on an instance; these overrides stay when the main changes.
Use Reset to undo overrides, Go to Main to find the main, or ⌥⌘B to detach an instance.

faq.q: Why can’t I move a layer inside an instance?
faq.a: Instance layers follow the main’s geometry. Change the layout in the main.

faq.q: What happens when I duplicate a main?
faq.a: You get a new, separate component.

features.why: Buttons, cards and icons repeat across a design, and updating each copy by hand is slow and error-prone. A main component is the single source; its instances follow every change while keeping the text, images and colors you change on them.
uses: Make a button component and place instances with different labels across screens.
Keep a navigation bar consistent on every page of a prototype.
Build a card with an image slot and swap the photo on each instance.
Update an icon once and see every screen pick up the change.

details.text: Makes a frame, or a framed selection, a main component. Shown with a diamond icon.
Places a linked copy, on this or another page. Duplicating an instance makes another instance; duplicating a main makes a new, separate component.
Shows how many instances are on this page, with Create Instance and Select Instances.

On an instance you can change text, fill, text style, stroke appearance, image, visibility, opacity, effects, name and text layout. The inspector lists what changed on each layer, and those changes stay when the main changes.
Reset Changes on This Layer, or Reset All to restore the whole instance, including swaps and property values.
Selects the main component, switching page if needed. If it's gone, the instance shows Main Component Missing.
Turns an instance into ordinary layers. Nested instances inside it stay linked.
Instance layers follow the main's geometry: they can't be deleted, moved in or out, framed or duplicated on their own. Change structure in the main; added and removed layers reach every instance.
Creating components and instances counts toward the free plan's layer limit.

tips: Give layers inside a main clear names. Overrides follow layer names when you swap variants.
Put Super Layout on the main so instances resize cleanly with longer text.
Keep mains on their own page and place instances everywhere else.
Write a description on the main: it shows as Markdown in every instance's Notes tab.

features.title: Variants and component properties
features.summary: Group variations of a component, such as size or state, and switch them on an instance.
steps: Select related components and choose Combine as Variants.
Name each property and value, for example State = Hover.
Add text, boolean or instance-swap properties to the main, with descriptions.
On an instance, switch variants and edit properties in the inspector.

faq.q: Which variant is the default?
faq.a: The one you mark as default, regardless of order.

faq.q: Can I document a component?
faq.a: Yes. Its description supports Markdown and shows in every instance’s Notes tab.

features.why: A button has sizes and states, and keeping each as a separate component makes them hard to switch. Variants group related components into one set, and component properties expose the parts people actually change, such as a label or an icon, as simple controls on each instance.
uses: Combine Default, Hover and Disabled buttons into one set with a State property.
Add a Boolean property that shows or hides a button's icon.
Expose a card's title as a Text property so instances edit it from the inspector.
Use an Instance Swap property to choose which icon sits inside a list row.

details.text: Select two or more main components. They're wrapped in a component set with a dashed purple outline. Names like "Size=Large, State=Hover" become variant properties; otherwise one "Property 1" takes each name.
Duplicates the last variant with a new value. Property names and values are editable.
Each variant property has a Default picker. New instances start as the variant matching every default, regardless of order.
Variant, Boolean, Text or Instance Swap, on a main or a component set. Boolean shows or hides a layer, Text changes a label and keeps its style, and Instance Swap replaces a nested instance.
On a layer inside the main, binds that layer to a new property. Choose None to unbind it.
Every property has a Description of up to 1,000 characters, shown under its control on instances. A component's own description renders as Markdown in the Notes tab.
On an instance or a nested instance, replaces its main. Switching a variant does the same. Layers with the same name path keep their overrides; the instance takes the new main's size.
From a variant, selects the set that contains it.

tips: Name components "Property=Value" before combining, and Mica builds the properties for you.
Keep layer names identical across variants so overrides carry over when you switch.
Prefer a Boolean property over a separate variant when only one layer shows or hides.
Document when to use each variant in property descriptions; designers see them right on the instance.

features.title: Variables and modes
features.summary: Store reusable colors, numbers, text and switches, and swap them with modes such as Light and Dark.
steps: Open Variables… from the board menu or Quick Actions and add a collection.
Add variables, then add modes and set each variable’s value per mode.
Select a layer and bind a property in its Variables section.
Choose a mode on a frame or page. Layers inside inherit the nearest mode.

faq.q: What can be bound?
faq.a: Fill, stroke, text color, opacity, size, gap, padding, font size, text, visibility, sizing modes and min/max sizes.

faq.q: Can a variable point to another?
faq.a: Yes, as an alias of the same type.

features.why: Hard-coded colors and sizes make theme changes a hunt through every layer. Variables store those values once, and modes such as Light and Dark let one design switch values everywhere at once.
uses: Define brand colors once and bind every fill and text color to them.
Preview a screen in Light and Dark by switching the frame's mode.
Keep spacing consistent with number variables for gap and padding.
Show the same mockup in several languages with string variables per mode.

details.text: Color (with alpha), Number, String, Boolean and Gradient.
Group variables into collections, each with its own modes. Variables can move between collections and keep their bindings. Name a variable "Group/Name" to group it.
Add Mode copies the last mode's values. There's no product cap on modes; the safety bounds are 1,000 modes and 10,000 variables. The first mode is the Default.
A value can point to another variable of the same type. Use Value turns it back into a plain value. Loops resolve to nothing.

In the layer's Variables section. Fill (color or gradient), stroke, text color, opacity, width, height, gap, padding, font size, text, visibility, width and height sizing, and min and max sizes. Detach removes a binding; mismatched types are ignored.
Frames pick a mode per collection, or Auto to inherit. Layers use the nearest frame's mode, then the page's, then the collection default.
In the Variables window, set the page's mode for each collection and a Background color variable.
Copies carry only the variables they use. Pasting into another board adds missing variables; existing ones win.

tips: Create a primitives collection (raw colors) and a semantic collection that aliases them, such as Background or Text Primary.
Bind gap and padding to number variables so spacing stays consistent, and change them in one place.
Set modes on frames for side-by-side previews, and on the page for the overall theme.
